summary: World models enable agents to plan and learn from imagined experience, but in an unfamiliar environment they must learn its mechanics from limited interaction. A mechanic is a rule for how an action or an interaction changes part of the environment.
takeaways: As a test bed, we build WARC (World model for ARC-AGI-3), a 35M-parameter vision transformer that is pretrained on other games and updates all of its parameters after each transition.
Each occurrence of a mechanic that the model observes is one exposure.
We ask how many exposures a world model needs to predict the effects of a new environment's mechanics.
